:::{#rem-algorithm-scope}
#### Procedures that are not algorithms here

By the definition of an [algorithm](#def-algorithm), every algorithm [computes](#def-computes) some function.
That holds because an algorithm has unambiguous steps and halts on every valid input.
A procedure that makes random choices can return different outputs for the same input.
A procedure that never halts returns no output for some inputs.
Neither computes a function, and neither is an algorithm in this sense,
although some texts call them algorithms.

:::
